en: The Sūtra on the Eight Kinds of Cultivating Merit Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmapāla and others— Śramaṇas of the Purple Robe and Grand Masters of Fan,
who were Imperially appointed as Chao-san-dafu and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial during the Western Heaven (India)— in accordance with the Imperial Edict.
I take refuge in all Buddhas!
May all Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas graciously accept me!
Then he spoke these verses:
"I now take refuge in supreme enlightenment, In the most sublime, pure Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
I generate the vast bodhicitta, To fully accomplish the benefit of both myself and others."
Confess and eliminate all unwholesome karma, Rejoice in the boundless masses of merit;
First, one should abstain from food for one day, And thereafter practice the eightfold observance for nourishing the assembly.
It should be known that the eight kinds of nourishing dharmas are the so-called Eight Precepts. The disciple should repeat them two or three times before the ācārya.
Having spoken this gāthā, he should next recite his own name:
"I am named [so-and-so]; I pray only that the ācārya will take me under his care."
From this moment forth, I shall give rise to pure faith until I sit at the site of enlightenment and attain perfect awakening.
I vow to take refuge in the Buddha, the supreme among two-legged beings;
I vow to take refuge in the Dharma, the supreme state free from desire.
I vow to take refuge in the Saṅgha, the most venerable among those who have attained self-mastery.
These Three Jewels are that to which I shall turn for refuge.
I, [Name], a lay follower (upāsaka) of pure faith, pray only that the Ācārya will remember me, uphold me, and look upon me with compassion.

From this day and this moment, having aroused a pure mind, until the end of this night and reaching the time when the sun first rises at dawn, one shall observe the eight precepts during that interval.

Namely: first, abstaining from taking life; second, abstaining from stealing; third, abstaining from unchaste conduct; fourth, abstaining from false speech; fifth, abstaining from drinking intoxicants; sixth, abstaining from eating at improper times; seventh, abstaining from adorning the body with flower garlands and from dancing, singing, and theatrical performances; eighth, abstaining from sitting or lying on high, wide, or large beds.
"I now renounce such matters as these, and vow never to abandon the eightfold merit of the pure prohibitive precepts.
He repeated this three times.
Furthermore, he said:

"I uphold the practice of the precepts to adorn my mind, causing it to be joyful; I extensively cultivate all corresponding superior practices, seeking to attain the fruit of Buddhahood to ultimate perfection."
And he spoke these verses:
“I have generated the supreme, non-dual mind, Acting as an uninvited friend for all sentient beings.
Through the virtuous practice of the sublime path to enlightenment, I shall attain Buddhahood and bring vast benefit to the world.”
By virtue of these wholesome deeds, may I attain perfect enlightenment in this very life before long;
may I preach the Dharma for the benefit of the world and explain the sufferings of the three realms of existence to all sentient beings.
The Sūtra on the Eight Kinds of Cultivating Merit Spoken by the Buddha.
